topIssues.title: feat(op-reth): implement interop tx pool filter and reorg eviction
topIssues.author: karlfloersch
topIssues.body:
## Summary

op-geth has two interop-related tx pool features that are not yet implemented in op-reth:

1. **Interop ingress filter** — validates interop transactions against the supervisor before admitting them to the mempool
2. **Interop tx eviction on reorg** — drops interop transactions from the pool when a reorg invalidates cross-chain state

Without these, op-reth nodes will accept interop transactions that reference invalid cross-chain messages, and reorgs can leave stale interop transactions in the mempool.

## What needs to be implemented

### 1. Transaction identification

An interop transaction is any transaction with access list entries targeting the CrossL2Inbox predeploy at `0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000022`. The storage keys under that address are the interop inbox entry hashes.

Reference: `core/types/interoptypes/interop.go` in op-geth (`TxToInteropAccessList`)

### 2. Ingress filter on tx pool add

Before adding an interop tx to the pool:
- Reject if the tx is older than 86400 seconds relative to the pending block time (expiry pre-check)
- Call `supervisor_checkAccessList(inboxEntries, "cross-unsafe", executingDescriptor)` and reject if it returns an error
- `ExecutingDescriptor` should be `{ChainID: node's chain ID, Timestamp: pending block time, Timeout: 86400}`

Reference: `core/txpool/ingress_filters.go` in op-geth

### 3. Periodic re-validation

Every ~12 seconds, re-check all interop transactions in the pool against the supervisor and drop those that now fail. Cross-chain state evolves over time, so transactions that were valid at admission may become invalid.

Reference: `filterTransactions()` / `FilterInterval` in op-geth `core/txpool/legacypool/legacypool.go`

### 4. Reorg eviction

When a reorg or head reset occurs, do **not** reinject interop transactions back into the pool. Filter them out from the "lost" transaction set before reinjection. After a reorg, cross-chain message references may be invalidated, so blindly reinserting interop txs is unsafe.

Reference: `filterInteropTxs()` in op-geth `core/txpool/legacypool/legacypool.go`

### 5. Block builder failsafe

Poll the supervisor via `admin_getFailsafeEnabled` every ~1 second. When the supervisor is in failsafe mode, reject **all** interop transactions from block building and evict them from the pool.

Reference: `miner/worker.go` (`commitTransaction`) and `miner/miner.go` (`startBackgroundInteropFailsafeDetection`) in op-geth

## op-geth reference files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `core/txpool/ingress_filters.go` | IngressFilter interface + interop filter impl |
| `core/types/interoptypes/interop.go` | Interop types, `TxToInteropAccessList()`, `ExecutingDescriptor` |
| `core/txpool/legacypool/legacypool.go` | Reorg eviction (`filterInteropTxs`), periodic re-check |
| `eth/interop.go` | `CheckAccessList()`, `CurrentInteropBlockTime()`, failsafe state |
| `eth/interop/interop.go` | RPC client for `supervisor_checkAccessList` |
| `eth/backend.go` | Wiring: creates filter, passes to tx pool |
| `miner/worker.go` | Block builder failsafe check |
| `miner/miner.go` | Background failsafe polling |
| `params/interop.go` | `InteropCrossL2InboxAddress` constant |

topIssues.title: dispute-mon: Multiple rollup node metrics
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
Once dispute-mon has support for reading from multiple rollup nodes (#11019), we need to expose additional metrics to support alerting when there are disagreements between nodes or some nodes failing. Each of these should be driven by adding fields to the `EnrichedGameData` to capture the data for a single game, then aggregated by adding a new [`Monitor`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/bde6a96e65d812f33681069009cdf3fa4f1f87d7/op-dispute-mon/mon/monitor.go#L19) in `gameMonitor` that aggregates the data across all games and then reports it to metrics ([`L2ChallengesMonitor`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/bde6a96e65d812f33681069009cdf3fa4f1f87d7/op-dispute-mon/mon/l2_challenges.go#L24) is an example of this kind of monitor implementation).

Metrics to report:
* Gauge of total number of endpoints that returned an error (other than not found) during the last update cycle - note this is the number of rpcs that had at least 1 failure, so if the same rpc gives an error on 10 games that still counts as 1.
* Gauge of total number of failures (other than not found) in the last update cycle. This counts each error from an rpc as a new event even if the rpc is the same (so one rpc giving 10 errors sets this to 10).
* Gauge of the total number of games where some nodes reported not found and others had the block in the last update cycle.
* Gauge of the total number of games where some nodes reported the output root as safe and others as unsafe in the last update cycle
* Gauge of the total number of games where nodes returned different expected output roots in the last update cycle

topIssues.title: [L2CM] Reuse ProxyAdmin tests on L2ProxyAdmin for backwards compatibility
topIssues.author: aliersh
topIssues.body:
**FMA follow-up (FM3):** `L2ProxyAdmin` replaces the existing `ProxyAdmin` predeploy. Other L2 contracts (`FeeVault`, `L1Withdrawer`, `FeeSplitter`) call `owner()` on it for access control. We need to verify that all existing `ProxyAdmin` functionality still works on `L2ProxyAdmin`.

Rather than writing a differential test from scratch, reuse the existing `ProxyAdmin.t.sol` ERC1967 test paths against `L2ProxyAdmin`. This proves backwards compatibility without duplicating test logic.

### Acceptance Criteria

- Existing `ProxyAdmin.t.sol` ERC1967 tests run successfully against `L2ProxyAdmin`
- Core functions verified: `owner()`, `upgrade()`, `upgradeAndCall()`, `changeProxyAdmin()`, `getProxyImplementation()`, `getProxyAdmin()`

### References

- [L2CM FMA — FM3: L2ProxyAdmin Backwards Compatibility Break](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/blob/main/security/fma-l2cm.md)
- Existing tests: `packages/contracts-bedrock/test/universal/ProxyAdmin.t.sol`

**Description**

op-dispute-mon has support for using multiple supernodes. This adds metrics for errors and disagreements between the nodes.

This PR was fully AI generated (with a review and prompted changes).

  New monitors
  - SuperNodeEndpointErrorsMonitor - tracks endpoints with errors
  - SuperNodeEndpointErrorCountMonitor - tracks total error count across all endpoints
  - MixedSuperAvailability - detects when some endpoints return "not found" while others succeed
  - MixedSuperSafety - detects when endpoints disagree on safety assessment
  - DifferentSuperRootMonitor - detects when endpoints return different super roots

  Prometheus metrics (metrics.go)
  - supernode_endpoint_errors - number of endpoints with errors
  - supernode_endpoint_error_count - total errors across all endpoints
  - mixed_super_availability_games - games with inconsistent block availability
  - mixed_super_safety_games - games with inconsistent safety assessments
  - different_super_root_games - games where endpoints returned different super roots

topPRs.title: op-acceptance-test: add flashblock acceptance tests for rule-based op-rbuilder
topPRs.author: mininny
topPRs.body:
**Description**

This PR adds new flashblock acceptance tests for op-rbuilder with rule-based ordering. 
This allows op-rbuilder to score individual transaction based on some specific ruleset, and include the transactions with the score ordering. 

See corresponding op-rbuilder PR for more detail: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-rbuilder/pull/1

To run these new tests, set flag like this: 
```
export OP_RBUILDER_EXEC_PATH=OP_RBUILDER_PATH
export ROLLUP_BOOST_EXEC_PATH=ROLLUP_BOOST_PATH
FLASHBLOCKS_RULES_TEST=1 just acceptance-test "" flashblocks
```

topPRs.title: docs(contracts): move l2 upgrade contracts spec from specs repo
topPRs.author: aliersh
topPRs.body:
This PR moves `l2-upgrades-2-contracts.md` from the specs repo into `packages/contracts-bedrock/specs/` as the first step of the specs colocation trial.

## Reason

Contract specifications maintained in a [separate repository](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs) fall out of sync with their implementations because updating them requires a separate PR in a separate repo, and reviewing implementation against a spec in a different location adds friction. Colocating the spec with the code enables AI-assisted review to flag contradictions between spec and implementation, letting a single PR update both when needed. This move is scoped to the L2CM contracts spec only, as a trial to evaluate whether colocation improves alignment without degrading dev velocity or spec readability.

## Changes

- Add `packages/contracts-bedrock/specs/l2-upgrades-2-contracts.md` with formal assumptions, invariants, and impact assessments for ConditionalDeployer, L2ProxyAdmin, and L2ContractsManager
